findings.title: Jeremiah 31:37: attributed quotation differs
findings.explanation: The Introduction’s Aleppo quotation has U+0591 etnaḥta; the cached doc-note has U+05BD Unicode METEG. The character’s encoding alone does not establish a narrow-sense meteg interpretation for this erroneous quotation. Both descriptions concern the unpointed gap for qere without ketiv. Ben adjudicated the doc-note on 2026-10-14 and requests etnaḥta, omission of the ḥolam dot, and optional inclusion of the orphan masorah circle. adjudications.json and jeremiah-31-37-adjudication.md retain the original and proposed quotations and contextual evidence. Chapter revision 3088451 is newer than Introduction revision 3087740; the closed #304 restoration of the formerly omitted phrase is independently checked and preserved. No source correction has been applied.

findings.title: Deuteronomy roster: nine declared, twelve words listed
findings.explanation: Ben specifies words as the items: six cite Leningrad and six cite Aleppo. Deuteronomy 32:10 contributes two words. The complete cached evidence accounts for 955/955 verses and 365/365 doc-notes. The 12 roster words match all 12 definite Aleppo/Leningrad vocal-sheva words in those notes. One possible omission remains: 3:22 has an uncertain Leningrad ḥataf ḥiriq, תְִּירָא֑וּם, whose blurred sign the note says may instead be a meteg. The additional 32:6 vowel is on yod in Firkovich B17, לְיֲהוָה֙, outside the named-manuscript scope. The 32:13 qere בָּ֣מֳתֵי retains morphological ḥataf qamats, outside the vocal-sheva policy. The edition also retains יֱהֹוִ֗ה at 3:24 and 9:26 and קׇדְקֳדֶֽךָ at 28:35; these are divine-name qere pointing and morphological ḥataf qamats, respectively. These four edition occurrences therefore do not add roster items. Of the 12 roster words, nine have the edition’s varika marker; 15:22 and both 32:10 words have plain sheva. Change (9 פריטים) to (12 פריטים). All 12 confirmed note words are listed, with no extra listed word; 3:22 remains an explicit uncertain omission. The cached evidence cannot exclude manuscript occurrences that were never documented.

findings.title: Lamentations 1:6: one and two are reversed
findings.explanation: The Introduction’s example gives מִן בַּת־ as ketiv and מִבַּת־ as qere. Its word counts reverse both the section’s category, כתיב תרתין מילין וקרי מילה חדה, and MAM’s special ketiv/qere template: ketiv מן בת; qere מִבַּת־. There is no doc-note at this verse. Keep the Introduction’s forms and pointing, and correct its counts as shown below.

findings.title: Proverbs 30:19: MAM illustration lacks the retained maqaf
findings.explanation: The Introduction's displayed MAM target has a space between the two atoms. The current note target has maqaf and explicitly agrees with Aleppo. The Introduction's own Aleppo quotation and maqaf policy agree with the note. The discrepancy belongs to the edition illustration; no competing Aleppo reading is established.

findings.title: Psalm 108:11: the quoted accent differs
findings.explanation: The Introduction quotation has U+0596 TIPEHA; the note has U+05AD DEHI in both its selected reading and the alternative attributed to Breuer. The nun-dagesh uncertainty agrees. The raw cache independently confirms the note quotation. This is an attributed-form disagreement, not a manuscript verdict.

findings.title: Psalms 57:9 and 108:3: secondary candidate accents differ
findings.explanation: Both sources prefer deḥi with meteg. The Introduction secondary option is deḥi with merkha; the notes instead propose terḥa with merkha. The difference appears in both the quoted codepoints and the explicit accent names. These are uncertain Aleppo candidate readings. The caches establish differing candidate sets; they do not select the actual manuscript reading.

findings.title: Named marks and letters disagree while quoted forms agree
findings.explanation: At Exodus 7:20 the Introduction names merkha where its specimen and the note have TEVIR. At Numbers 16:27 it places segol on qof while the specimen and note place it on resh. At Numbers 22:23 it names bet instead of the note's dalet; the specimen has no bet. At Deuteronomy 28:27 the direction reverses: the Introduction names tet correctly, while the note calls that letter tav in its final clause. The quoted qere has tet and no tav. These are description discrepancies, not new manuscript readings. The uncertainty qualifier at Numbers 22:23 requires separate attention.

findings.title: Daniel 2:17: meteg differs in the Leningrad quotation
findings.explanation: The explicitly Leningrad-attributed Introduction specimen includes U+05BD under dalet; the note specimen omits it. Both describe the missing yod dagesh, and that phenomenon agrees. The extra meteg is a supported difference between the attributed quotations. Raw and parsed note captures agree. No notation-policy limitation was found in this local context, and the manuscript reading remains unverified.

findings.title: Daniel 5:7: yod differs in the Leningrad ketiv quotation
findings.explanation: The Introduction's explicitly Leningrad-attributed ketiv includes a yod after nun; the note's Leningrad ketiv omits that yod. The raw note agrees with the parsed note, and direct codepoint checks establish the consonantal difference. This is a supported source-quoted spelling discrepancy, with the manuscript reading still unverified.

findings.title: Daniel 7:9: the starred edition reading is reversed
findings.explanation: The decision list places the edition-selection star on the Leningrad full-first-yod form. The main spelling row and current MAM target select the defective-first-yod form instead. The note explicitly distinguishes these source spellings. This is an internal Introduction selection reversal corroborated by current edition evidence; the Leningrad manuscript claim itself agrees.

findings.title: Chapter 4: spelling cross-references lack decision-list entries
findings.explanation: The main list has 26 orange rows referring readers to the decision list, but that list has 17 verse entries; nine orange rows have no counterpart. Three representative missing cases explicitly have at least three named rejected witnesses in the notes, fitting the inclusion rule at ch4:L311. Daniel 4:33 names Leningrad, B1 and Or 2212; Daniel 5:29 names Leningrad, Sh1 and B1; Daniel 8:8 names Leningrad, Q-M and T451. This establishes one internal list-coverage family, without proving the complete census required by the general rule. All nine missing IDs are retained in ch4-spelling-batch.json.

findings.title: Psalm 39:13: merkha and meteg exchange positions in the Leningrad quotation
findings.explanation: Two identical Introduction entries put MERKHA (U+05A5) on shin and METEG (U+05BD) on ayin in the explicitly Leningrad-attributed form. The raw and parsed note put METEG on shin and MERKHA on ayin. Maqaf and sheva agree. The note separately retains Aleppo ḥataf uncertainty; this finding concerns the Leningrad quotation and leaves the physical reading unverified.

findings.title: Psalm 17:14: Leningrad candidate maqaf conflicts with the Introduction
findings.explanation: The Introduction quotes two Leningrad candidates without MAQAF (U+05BE) and explicitly says there is no maqaf. Both note candidates include maqaf; the note also says meteg, merkha and maqaf. The first candidate is attributed to the typist and the second to Dotan, whose uncertainty is retained. The Sh1/Q13 statement agrees. Raw-template serialization was checked independently; no manuscript image was consulted.

findings.title: Three Torah doc-notes have letter-label or source-list inconsistencies
findings.explanation: Numbers 9:7 calls the selected full-YOD form full VAV, although that atom has yod and no vav. Deuteronomy 32:34 calls its full-VAV form full YOD, although the atom has vav and no yod. At Deuteronomy 6:21 the note lists Leningrad both among the implicit MAM defective-vav witnesses and in an explicit full-vav alternative; its final prose supports the full-vav Leningrad form quoted by the Introduction. Faithful raw bodies and selected target forms confirm all three. These note prose/source-list defects remain separate from physical manuscript readings. Ben confirmed the Numbers 9:7 vav-to-yod wording correction on 2026-10-14; adjudications.json retains the exact stored punctuation and proposed wording. No source correction has been applied. Ben also confirmed the inverse Deuteronomy 32:34 yod-to-vav wording correction on 2026-10-14; its exact stored punctuation and proposed wording are retained in adjudications.json. Ben adjudicated Deuteronomy 6:21 on 2026-10-14: remove only bare ל from the initial list, preserving ל1. The repeated note statements favor this direction, and Ben independently inspected the manuscript and found it pretty clearly plene-vav. Damage/erasure causes remain uncertain; the precise proposed note is retained without any upstream edit.

findings.title: Isaiah 10:15: Aleppo spelling quotations omit different yods
findings.explanation: The table explicitly identifies its middle column as the Aleppo form. Its specimen lacks the second yod; the current raw/parsed note lacks the first yod and expressly names the first yod as the partly erased letter. The starred edition form agrees with current MAM. This is a positional spelling-quotation disagreement, with the physical manuscript reading still unverified. The earlier Introduction summary at ch5:L47 brackets the same second-yod position, while L56’s prose names the first yod, matching the note.

findings.title: Joshua 14:7: the Introduction stars a meteg that the edition omits

Raw evidence confirms the target and candidate relation. Selection and certainty have changed; the caches do not settle the fine mark in the manuscript.

The Psalms roster has 172 form items against171 declared items, but item-count and ḥataf-occurrence-count are kept distinct.

The current raw/parsed note distinguishes the two vowels correctly and retains uncertainty about Aleppo. Both alternative forms agree; the defect is the Introduction's second vowel label.

Daniel 5:3 and Nehemiah 12:47 retain transcription/question qualifiers absent from the Introduction. Physical readings remain unresolved.

uncertainty.title: Deuteronomy 5:13: reading-strand assignments exceed the note
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction assigns the two quoted marks to reading strands more specifically than the note's explicit Leningrad description of munaḥ and merkha. The quoted marks themselves are corroborated. Keep the strand assignment as a separate source-scope question.

uncertainty.title: Shared or incidental explanation differences
uncertainty.explanation: Song of Songs 4:16 names lamed, although the difference between the displayed MAM and Leningrad specimens is dagesh on zayin; lamed is undotted in both. At Lamentations 4:7 both specimens encode segol on shin while the descriptions discuss qamats and the note preserves uncertainty about close dots. These are explanation questions, not independent disagreements about the manuscript reading.

uncertainty.title: Spelling specimens carry incidental accent differences
uncertainty.explanation: Chapter 4 explicitly defines its star as the selected spelling. It does not assert complete pointing through that star alone. Nehemiah 9:37's missing second telisha and Daniel 7:15's unnamed rejected accent therefore remain incidental quotation questions; the central spelling selections agree.

uncertainty.title: Spelling notes support less-specific source claims
uncertainty.explanation: The local spelling evidence agrees, but the notes do not establish every source detail: a small-versus-large Masorah distinction; specifically small Aleppo Masorah rather than generic Aleppo Masorah; own-Masorah-L support underlying a surprising form; and Leningrad attribution of Daniel 5:16's ketiv. The batch ledger retains these as unsupported subclaims, without upgrading note silence into contradiction.

uncertainty.title: Torah spelling and joining specimens: incidental pointing and certainty
uncertainty.explanation: The two incidental meteg specimens retain quotation scope. Numbers 1:10 and 10:19 explicitly document joined/spaced Leningrad forms; whether earlier uncertainty was unwarranted cannot be dated from the cache. Deuteronomy 32:6's Leningrad quotation omits the yod SHEVA explicitly present and described in the note. The ḥolam policy does not explain that SHEVA omission. Joining agrees; complete-quotation intent and physical truth remain open.

uncertainty.title: Special-letter lists: precise Masorah subclaims exceed local notes
uncertainty.explanation: Isaiah 44:14 specifies small Aleppo Masorah while its note names generic Aleppo Masorah. Psalm 27:13 associates a six-dot Leningrad form with small Leningrad Masorah; the corresponding note gives that form for LS1 and specifically cites small Aleppo Masorah. The form evidence agrees, and both positive source claims could coexist. The precise subclaims remain unsupported locally rather than contradicted.

uncertainty.title: Size-list specimens omit incidental meteg or legarmeh structure
uncertainty.explanation: Chapter 5 defines its star as the size performed in MAM. All three selected sizes agree. Complete Ruth/Esther targets retain legarmeh and both Psalm 77:8 helper branches retain initial meteg; incomplete survey text must not hide those marks. Full pointing-quotation intent remains editorial.

uncertainty.title: Exodus 7:13: implicit Leningrad meteg agreement has uncertain scope
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction's Leningrad specimen has no meteg. The note's target has meteg and its implicit agreement includes Leningrad, but the following explanatory list specifically names other witnesses for the yod meteg. Keep this conflict in clause scope separate from the explanatory PATAH typo; neither cache settles the actual manuscript reading.

uncertainty.title: Ḥataf rosters: source scope and inclusion questions
uncertainty.explanation: Nine unsigled specimens have explicit Aleppo note counterparts, consistent with the enclosing Aleppo-or-Leningrad heading; missing item sigla are not an evidence block for those nine. Two Jeremiah qere specimens still cross notes documenting ketiv; Ezekiel 17:17's Leningrad claim lacks a matching named-L clause. Inclusion of the additional Proverbs 30:17 Leningrad ḥataf remains editorial.

uncertainty.title: Deuteronomy 20:1: uncertain seder versus error wording
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction calls Dotan's bracketed seder an error, while the current note describes it as uncertain and only proposes how an error might have arisen. Dotan's source was not consulted. Preserve the difference in description strength without resolving the manuscript or historical source.

uncertainty.title: Poetic numerical totals need a semantic population definition
uncertainty.explanation: Current MAM has 4465 poetic verses, 2679 DEHI verses and 423 OLEH verses. The current closed MAM-simple disjunctive extractor independently reproduces both memberships; helper/qamats alternatives preserve them. A complete atom-stream predicate partitions the 423 OLEH cases into 368 same-atom and 55 two-atom cases, with zero unmatched cases. All 55 current two-atom verse memberships match the Introduction's three lists exactly: 38 joined by maqaf, 17 spaced. The Introduction's 2685/421 totals still lack a cached source-membership/counting contract. Current cached WLC does not reproduce those totals; its limited scanner recovery is not a complete grammatical census.

uncertainty.title: Long legarmeh roster: locators, selection and historical source scope
uncertainty.explanation: Only two of the six existing main targets lacking selected legarmeh are resolved by wrong-reference correction: 2 Samuel 15:2 to 15:30 and Song 3:3 to Ruth 3:3. Song 3:13 to Ruth 3:13 repairs a nonexistent target and is not a third of those six. Four existing selected absences remain: 1 Samuel 11:9, 11:12; Zechariah 10:12; 1 Chronicles 18:10. The historical Wick population and physical witnesses remain unverified. This corrects the maintained research explanation, not Scripture input.

uncertainty.title: Isaiah 44:24: physical maqaf versus ketiv display convention
uncertainty.explanation: The Leningrad ketiv quotation contains maqaf but its parenthesis says there is none because the qere is a single atom. The Introduction and Aleppo clause agree. It remains unclear whether the L clause uses a reconstructed display separator while describing physical punctuation; literal glyph/prose mismatch is recorded without a manuscript contradiction verdict.

uncertainty.title: Poetic-design quotations: incidental vowels, rafe and accent glyphs
uncertainty.explanation: Other Introduction passages agree with the notes for Psalm 6:3's qamats, Psalm 74:5's ḥataf and Psalm 68:18's rafe, while the design lists differ literally. Proverbs 8:34's other entry retains ATNAH HAFUKH and doubt; the design list uses GALGAL and a certain star. These are concrete internal quotation/qualification differences. The central design predicates agree. Complete manuscript-quotation intent and physical readings remain open; do not inflate them into four new central-feature alarms.

uncertainty.title: Catalogue classification and counting scope need clarification
uncertainty.explanation: Chapter 2 lists three cases and the appendix four, adding 2 Samuel 8:3. Both describe templates and Masorah notes; no manuscript-note versus template-use distinction is established. Chapter 2’s first-word criterion may explain Samuel’s exclusion because בנהר remains its first qere word and פרת is added. Both also list Samuel as qere without ketiv. The note distinguishes Aleppo’s two-word qere from the other named sources, but neither a manuscript basis nor an exclusion rule is specified for chapter 2’s total. Establish classification and counting scope before treating the totals as contradictory. The separate 2 Samuel 21:12 two-word/three-word qere-note question remains unresolved. The 19-line membership comparison records 15 matches and four differences under current template identity; those differences do not themselves establish counting errors.

controls.title: Proverbs 30:5: Aleppo's omitted revia dot agrees
controls.explanation: Both sources attribute the omitted revia dot to Aleppo. Ordering of the Introduction's displayed accents differs from MAM's order; that literal encoding difference is not a competing manuscript reading.

controls.title: Job 11:6: oleh position agrees
controls.explanation: Both sources attribute the same oleh position to Aleppo. The printed alternative is explicitly distinguished. Source strings retain their original mark order.
